Hello — welcome to Chiang Mai. Below are top things to do within about an hour’s drive, followed by two viable multi-leg transport routes in JSON and a short list of five absolute must-see attractions across Thailand.

Within an hour’s drive of Chiang Mai (mountains, waterfalls, temples, attractions)
- Doi Suthep (Wat Phra That Doi Suthep): Chiang Mai’s signature mountain temple — golden chedi, sweeping city views, easy 30–45-minute drive from the Old City. Ideal at sunrise or sunset.
- Doi Pui and Hmong Hilltribe Village: Higher, cooler forested ridge above Doi Suthep with viewpoints, short trails, and cultural visits (40–60 minutes by car).
- Bua Thong Sticky Waterfalls (Mae Taeng): Limestone cascades you can climb barefoot — unique and family-friendly, about 1 hour north.
- Huay Kaew Waterfall & Mon Cham: Small cascades and gardens; Mon Cham (on Doi Suthep-Pui ridge) offers terraced farmland views and tea/flower farms (30–50 min).
- Mae Sa Waterfall & Mae Sa Valley: Multi-tiered waterfall, botanical gardens and elephant camps in the same valley — 30–45 minutes.
- Queen Sirikit Botanic Garden (Mae Rim): World-class conservatory and canopy walk, good for a relaxed half-day (45–55 minutes).
- Doi Khun Tan (National Park): Real mountain hiking with rainforest and viewpoints—trailheads are ~60 min away; tuk-tuk + trek.
- Wat Umong: Forest temple with tunnels and a tranquil atmosphere within city-edge mountain slopes — 20 minutes.
- San Kamphaeng Hot Springs: Natural hot baths for a soothing stop on the way to northern attractions (~45–60 minutes).

Practical notes: rent a car or hire a local driver for flexibility (many mountain roads are narrow), leave early to avoid midday heat and afternoon monsoon showers (May–Oct). Dress modestly at temples; bring good shoes for waterfalls and clear plastic bags for wet items.

Five MUST-SEE attractions across Thailand (the absolute best)
1) Chiang Mai — Wat Phra That Doi Suthep & surrounding mountains
2) Luang Prabang (Northern Laos) — While outside Thailand, it pairs perfectly with Northern Thailand itineraries (historic temples & Mekong). 
3) Bangkok — Grand Palace, Wat Pho and a longtail boat ride on the Thonburi canals
4) Phang Nga Bay / Phi Phi Islands / Similan Islands — world-class marine scenery and snorkeling (Phuket/Andaman gateway)
5) Ayutthaya Historical Park — unforgettable ruins and a deep sense of Thai history
